blogs.title: Reinforcement Learning Meets Large Language Models: A Primer for Everyday Readers
blogs.description: An introductory post that explains why reinforcement learning (RL) is becoming essential for scaling language models, how it works at a high level, and what challenges arise when trying to train gigantic models with RL.

blogs.title: From Tokens to Whole Sentences: Why Sequence‑Level Thinking Saves Giant LLMs from Collapse
blogs.description: A deep‑dive into the core problem with previous methods like GRPO—applying importance weights at the token level—and how this mismatch leads to high‑variance noise and model collapse. The article uses intuitive analogies to illustrate why aligning the unit of optimization (the reward) with the unit of importance sampling (the entire response) matters.

blogs.title: Introducing Group Sequence Policy Optimization (GSPO): The Algorithm Redefining RL for LLMs
blogs.description: A step‑by‑step walkthrough of GSPO’s design, from its sequence‑level importance ratio to its novel clipping mechanism. The post demystifies the math behind GSPO while keeping the explanation accessible, showing how it builds on and corrects earlier RL algorithms.

blogs.title: Stabilizing Mixture‑of‑Experts Models Without Routing Replay: GSPO’s Secret Sauce
blogs.description: Explains the unique instability challenges posed by Mixture‑of‑Experts (MoE) architectures during RL training, why GRPO needed a cumbersome “Routing Replay” workaround, and how GSPO’s focus on sequence likelihood naturally sidesteps expert‑activation volatility.

blogs.title: Clipping More Tokens, Yet Learning Faster: Counter‑Intuitive Efficiency Gains with GSPO
blogs.description: Analyzes why GSPO’s practice of clipping entire responses—resulting in a higher fraction of “clipped” tokens—actually leads to better sample efficiency compared to token‑level clipping in GRPO. The article uses visual analogies and simple statistics to make the concept clear.

blogs.title: Simplifying RL Infrastructure: Using Inference Engine Likelihoods Directly with GSPO
blogs.description: Discusses practical engineering benefits of GSPO, such as eliminating the need to recompute old‑policy likelihoods on training hardware. It shows how sequence‑level likelihoods tolerate precision differences between training and inference engines, enabling more flexible and cost‑effective pipelines.

blogs.title: From Theory to Triumph: How GSPO Powered the New Qwen3 Models
blogs.(description): "A case study that follows the journey from experimental results to real product impact—highlighting reward curves, benchmark gains (AIME'24, LiveCodeBench, CodeForces), and how GSPO enabled continuous performance improvements in the latest Qwen3 language models."
